interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is documented. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 36.15 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 27.12–45.19 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology indicates a Gleason 4+5 (ISUP grade group 5) and pathological stage pT3a. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins, no invasion of the seminal vesicles, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no lymph node metastasis, as documented by the surgical pathology report: "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 4+5 (ISUP grade group 5), pathological stage pT3a. Extraprostatic extension was present; surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." This is counterbalanced by the preoperative PSA of 3.7. Nodal status is documented as "there was no lymph node metastasis." The biopsy report is missing Gleason pattern and ISUP details. The prognosis is supported by the negative margins and absence of nodal disease. However, the postoperative PSA is not recorded, meaning biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Missing nodal sampling, although not explicitly noted as missing in the provided data structure, widens uncertainty regarding complete staging. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are the critical information needed to revise this prognosis.
